dmm-2020-devil-02.title: Official value and how to get it
dmm-2020-devil-02.body:
Official value: **13615**.

Estimate: the $n$th prime is about $n(\ln n+\ln\ln n-1)$. With $n=10312020$: $\ln n\approx16.15$, $\ln\ln n\approx2.78$, so $p_n\approx1.0312\times10^7\cdot17.93\approx1.85\times10^8$ and $\sqrt{p_n}\approx13600$. A sieve gives $p_{10312020}=185362007$, whose square root is $13614.77\approx13615$.

dmm-2020-devil-05.title: Official value and how to compute it
dmm-2020-devil-05.body:
Official value: **40.524**.

The operation "$V\to1/V$" makes the expectation non-linear, so one tracks the whole distribution of $V$: start with $\{100:1\}$ and, for $20$ rounds, replace each value $v$ (probability $\pi$) by $v+20$ and $1/v$, each with probability $\pi/2$. Summing $v\cdot\pi$ at the end gives $40.524$.

dmm-2020-devil-08.title: Search the decimal expansion
dmm-2020-devil-08.body: The official key gives **7377**. Computing the digits of $\pi$ (for example with Machin's formula $\pi=16\arctan\frac15-4\arctan\frac1{239}$) and searching shows that the block $2020$ first appears starting at decimal place $7285$ (the digits there read $\ldots742\,2020\,203\ldots$), i.e. after $7284$ digits. For an estimation question any guess in the right range is scored by closeness; the stored official number differs from the computed position.
